scheme_name: Primary Cooperative Agriculture and Rural Development Bank: For Poultry Development
description:
The Primary Cooperative Agriculture and Rural Development Bank scheme for Poultry Development is an initiative aimed at enhancing the poultry sector in India.

This scheme was launched in 2007 under the Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers' Welfare.

The primary objective of this scheme is to promote poultry farming as a sustainable livelihood option for rural farmers.

It aims to increase the production of poultry products such as eggs and meat.

The scheme also seeks to improve the income levels of rural households through poultry farming.

The government has set a target to increase poultry production by 10 percent annually.

The scheme is designed to provide financial assistance to farmers for setting up poultry units.

Farmers can receive loans up to INR 10 lakh for establishing poultry farms.

The interest rate on these loans is subsidized at 4 percent per annum.

The repayment period for these loans is typically 5 to 7 years.

The scheme also provides training and capacity-building programs for farmers.

These programs are aimed at educating farmers about modern poultry farming techniques.

The benefits of the scheme include increased employment opportunities in rural areas.

It also contributes to the nutritional security of the population through increased egg and meat production.

Eligibility for this scheme is primarily targeted at small and marginal farmers.

Farmers must be members of a cooperative society to qualify for the benefits.

The age limit for applicants is generally between 18 to 60 years.

There are no specific educational qualifications required for eligibility.

The income criteria for eligibility is set at a maximum annual income of INR 1.5 lakh.

The application process involves several steps.

Farmers must first approach their local Primary Cooperative Agriculture and Rural Development Bank.

They need to fill out an application form detailing their project proposal.

Required documents include proof of identity, proof of land ownership, and a project report.

Farmers must also submit a certificate of membership from the cooperative society.

Once the application is submitted, it is reviewed by the bank officials.

The bank may conduct a field visit to assess the viability of the project.

If approved, the loan amount is disbursed in a phased manner.

The timeline for loan disbursement typically ranges from 30 to 60 days after approval.

The scheme is implemented through a network of cooperative banks across the country.

The implementing authority is the National Cooperative Development Corporation.

Farmers can contact the local cooperative bank for more information.

The scheme is part of a larger effort to boost the rural economy.

It aligns with the government's vision of doubling farmers' income by 2022.

The poultry sector is a significant contributor to the agricultural GDP.

As of 2021, the poultry sector accounted for approximately 1.1 percent of the total GDP.

The government has also introduced various other initiatives to support the poultry industry.

These include the National Livestock Mission launched in 2014.

The National Livestock Mission aims to enhance livestock production and productivity.

In 2020, the government allocated INR 900 crore for the development of the poultry sector.

This funding is aimed at improving infrastructure and providing better facilities for poultry farmers.

The scheme encourages the use of modern technology in poultry farming.

Farmers are trained in biosecurity measures to prevent diseases in poultry.

The government also promotes the use of quality feed and vaccines.

The poultry development scheme has shown positive results in various states.

States like Andhra Pradesh and Tamil Nadu have seen significant growth in poultry production.

The scheme has also contributed to women's empowerment in rural areas.

Many women have taken up poultry farming as a source of income.

The government provides additional support for women entrepreneurs in this sector.

The scheme is continuously monitored for its effectiveness and impact.

Feedback from beneficiaries is collected to improve the scheme.

The government aims to expand the reach of the scheme to more farmers.

This includes increasing awareness about the benefits of poultry farming.

The scheme has the potential to transform the livelihoods of rural families.

It encourages sustainable agricultural practices and enhances food security.

The poultry development initiative is a crucial component of rural development.

It plays a vital role in achieving self-sufficiency in poultry production.

The scheme is expected to create a ripple effect in the rural economy.

Increased poultry production leads to job creation in related sectors.

These include feed production, veterinary services, and processing industries.

The government is committed to supporting the poultry sector through various policies.

This includes providing subsidies for feed and veterinary care.

The scheme is part of a broader strategy to enhance agricultural productivity.

It reflects the government's commitment to improving the living standards of rural farmers.

The poultry development scheme is a step towards achieving sustainable rural development.

It aims to create a robust poultry sector that can compete globally.

Farmers are encouraged to form cooperatives to enhance their bargaining power.

The cooperative model helps in pooling resources and sharing knowledge.

The government also facilitates access to markets for poultry products.

This ensures that farmers get fair prices for their produce.

The scheme is aligned with the Sustainable Development Goals.

It contributes to ending hunger and promoting sustainable agriculture.

The poultry development initiative is a comprehensive approach to rural upliftment.

It addresses various challenges faced by farmers in the poultry sector.

The scheme is expected to evolve based on changing needs and circumstances.

The government remains committed to supporting the poultry industry for future growth.
